newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MPs pass new mandate for Iraq air patrols.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MPs pass new mandate for Iraq air patrols.

text.p: Turkish MPs on Thursday approved a six-month extension of a U.S.-led aerial surveillance operation to protect the Kurdish regions of northern Iraq.
"Parliament has decided to extend the mandate by six months," speaker Hasan Korkmazcan told the assembly.
The mandate for the joint U.S.-British force, based at the Incirlik air base in southern Turkey, was last renewed in December 1996.
Northern Watch planes have been patrolling the skies of northern Iraq to protect Kurds from any attack by Baghdad since the Gulf War ended in 1991.
The operation, previously named Provide Comfort, was redubbed Northern Watch following the withdrawal of French aircraft at the end of last year.
Turkish deputies have often complained the air shield helped to create a power vacuum exploited by Kurdish rebels using bases in northern Iraq.
"There is still an authority vacuum in northern Iraq," leftist deputy Ali Topuz was quoted as saying by Anatolian news agency, "Turkey must put itself on a path of normalising ties with Iraq."
Turkish security forces, involved for six weeks in an anti-rebel operation in northern Iraq, have now mostly withdrawn from the region.
